chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman, from Muhammad ibn ʿUdhafir, who said:
Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: The supererogatory salat is like a gift; whenever it is brought, it is accepted. So perform of it whatever you wish earlier, and delay of it whatever you wish.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand them as a kind of concession for one who knows that if he does not perform them earlier, he will become occupied from them and will not be able to make them up; this is indicated by that.

key_terms.الْهَدِيَّةِ: a gift, used here to indicate ready acceptance when offered
key_terms.صَلَاةُ التَّطَوُّعِ: supererogatory salat performed voluntarily in addition to obligatory prayer
key_terms.فَقَدِّمْ: perform earlier or advance in time
key_terms.قَضَائِهَا: making it up after its proper time

ai.seo_question: Can the nawafil of the day be performed earlier or delayed if one fears missing them?
ai.summary: This hadith states that supererogatory salat has flexibility in its timing, likening it to a gift that is accepted whenever it is offered. The concluding legal note explains that such reports are understood as a concession for a person who fears being distracted from performing these nawafil later and being unable to make them up.
